sections.html:
Greenwich is the state's far southwest corner, and the 2020 census put its population at 63,518. New York State is the western border (Port Chester, Rye Brook, North Castle), Stamford is the eastern neighbor and Long Island Sound is the southern edge. ZIP codes are 06830, 06831, 06870 and 06878.

One town government taxes everything, yet buyers think in sections. Cos Cob, Old Greenwich and Riverside carry their own postal names, Byram, Glenville, Pemberwick and Rock Ridge are distinct villages, and the Back Country, Mid-Country, Belle Haven and Mianus are informal labels that agents use all the time. Two things shape value more than most: the commute (four Metro-North stations, with express trains to Grand Central in about 50 minutes and locals in about 60) and water. Old Greenwich, Riverside and Byram hug the shore, which makes flood zone status a routine question, and the Back Country above the Merritt Parkway collects more snow than the coast does.

For one specific address, call Planning and Zoning or the Wetlands office.

Greenwich rolls real estate, personal property and motor vehicle tax into a single bill. It goes out in June with payment due July 1, and in the latest cycle on the Tax Collector's page the bill went delinquent after August 3. Mailing and delinquency dates shift between years, so trust the bill in your hand.

Visit the Tax Collector in Town Hall, 101 Field Point Road, Room 145, weekdays 8:30 am to 3:30 pm, or phone 203-622-7891.

Way to payFee
In person or by mail (check, money order, cash in person)No fee
Online, electronic funds transfer$2.00 per transaction, paid to the vendor
Online, card, Apple Pay or Google Pay2.50 percent of the payment, paid to the vendor
Returned payment$20.00 plus possible interest

Interest on a late real estate bill runs to a stated date, and a lien goes on any property that still has a balance in May. Behind on the bill? Get a payoff number from the office first, then pick your closing date.

sections.h2: Where to file a Greenwich assessment appeal
sections.html:
Appeals go to an elected body, the Board of Assessment Appeals. The Assessor's Office turns away appeal forms, which catches out owners who assume the assessor is the right door. The Board's page has the form and the email address, boardofassessmentappeals@greenwichct.org.

Under Connecticut General Statutes section 12-111, real estate and personal property filings close in February at 5:00 pm. The 2025 Grand List cutoff was February 20, with in-person hearings at Town Hall that March. The 2026 Grand List will have its own posted date, so confirm it with the Board before relying on any day.

  • An appeal disputes the assessment alone. The mill rate comes from the Board of Estimate and Taxation each May.
  • The result can be a higher value, a lower one or no change, and notices go out roughly two weeks after the final hearing.
  • A dissatisfied owner has 60 days from the notice to apply to Connecticut Superior Court.
  • The Board may decline hearings on commercial, industrial, utility or apartment property assessed above $1,000,000.

Its five members are elected every two years, in odd-numbered years.

Recording a deed in Greenwich triggers a state filing, Form OP-236, signed by the seller or the seller's attorney. The town code to enter is 057. Consideration of $2,000 or more is taxed unless the transfer is exempt.

The exempt list on the Department of Revenue Services tax information page names transfers between spouses, a deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence, and a principal residence sold for less than the mortgages and tax liens against it. Ask your closing agent or the Town Clerk's office which line fits your deal.

sections.h2: Selling a Greenwich house with taxes owed
sections.html:
Owing tax does not rule out selling. The balance is subtracted from what you receive at closing, so your real task is learning the number early. Here is a workable order.

  1. Request a payoff on the real estate account from the Tax Collector, interest included.
  2. Ask if a lien has been recorded. Balances get liened in May, and the release must be arranged as part of closing.
  3. Hand the payoff to your closing attorney, who builds it into the settlement statement.
  4. Set the closing date after the lien question is answered, not before.

A lien is not the end of the road. Once the payoff is paid at closing, the lien is released and the buyer receives clear title. Allow a little extra time on the calendar for the release paperwork, particularly if closing falls close to a month-end or a holiday.

Bring the bill, a photo ID and, for an estate, the papers showing who may sign. Because a missed May date can turn a small balance into a lien, even owners who are only slightly behind should call early.

sections.h2: Reading your bill and your record
sections.html: Before you call any office, put three things on the table: the latest tax bill, the assessment notice and the property record. Check the bill for the account number, since the Tax Collector will ask for it. Check the record for square footage, bathroom count and any addition, because an error there carries straight into the assessment and gives you something concrete to bring to the Board. Write down every call: who you spoke with, the date and the figure quoted. A written payoff is what your closing attorney actually needs, and a verbal number from last month will not do.

Coastal sections, village centers and the Back Country make Greenwich a town where the street decides the story. Houses needing repairs sit longer on the open market. Estates often wait on probate before anyone can list. Owners behind on tax may face a May lien and need a closing date that clears it.

Some owners choose a cash sale for the certain closing date. The buyer accepts the house as-is, you skip the repair list, and open tax is taken from the proceeds. Weigh that against what fixing the house and carrying it through another bill would cost.

sections.h2: Beaches, water and what buyers ask
sections.html: The town runs four Sound beaches: Greenwich Point, Byram Beach, Island Beach and Great Captain Island, all opened to non-residents after the 2001 Leydon v. Greenwich ruling. For a seller the shoreline comes down to flood zone mapping, drainage and the age of docks or seawalls. Waterfront buyers usually want insurance history before they offer, so collect it before you list. A short folder with flood certificates, past claims and repair receipts for any seawall or dock saves a week of back and forth later.

faqs.q: When are Greenwich property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment is due July 1, and the bill turns delinquent a few weeks later. Check the Tax Collector's page each year, since mailing and delinquency dates can change.

faqs.q: Where do I file a Greenwich assessment appeal?
faqs.a: With the Board of Assessment Appeals, not the Assessor. The Board's email is boardofassessmentappeals@greenwichct.org.

faqs.q: Who sets the Greenwich mill rate?
faqs.a: The Board of Estimate and Taxation sets it in May. An assessment appeal does not change the rate.

faqs.q: What happens to Greenwich real estate that stays delinquent?
faqs.a: Interest builds up to a set date, and any property with a balance is liened in May. Call the Tax Collector for a payoff before you set a closing date, and ask whether a lien paper has already been recorded against the house.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Greenwich house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid tax comes out of the proceeds at closing, and a cash sale can close on a date you choose.
